Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

regular adjective

at fixed times, steady

also regularly, at regular intervals, on a regular basis, a regular habit

classical

Liv. 44.37: lūnae dēfectiō statīs temporibus fit (Lewis & Short, s.v. sistō)
Liv. 42.32.2: statō locō statīsque diēbus

status, stata, statum

adjective, declension

fixed, appointed, regular (of times and days)

Used in set phrases: status diēs, statum tempus, stata sacrificia; Pliny calls fevers that come back at regular intervals statae febrēs (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • assiduus, assidua, assiduum — constant, regular, always there

    adjective; adverb assiduē, regularly, declension · also used · classical · Traupman 60, 370: assiduē, regularly

    Of someone who keeps at a thing or is always present; assiduē is “continually, regularly”. Its first sense is “settled on the land” (Lewis & Short).

  • ōrdinārius, ōrdināria, ōrdinārium — according to the usual order, regular

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · cōnsulēs ōrdināriī, the regular consuls (Lewis & Short)

    Not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short): an official word, the regular as against the extraordinary.

Examples

  • Sī tū haec assiduē faciēs, tū quidem eris āthlēta summus.

    If you do this regularly, you’ll surely become a top athlete.Traupman 60

  • Medicāmentum statīs hōrīs sūmendum est.

    The medicine is to be taken at regular times.composed

See also normal, pattern, proper.

SourcesLewis & Short: sisto · Lewis & Short: assiduus · Lewis & Short: ordinarius

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 60, 370.
